skill.name: network-101
skill.description: Guides authorized network service lab setup and testing for HTTP, HTTPS, SNMP, and SMB on Linux or Windows systems.
skill.summary: Configure and test common network services in isolated security training labs.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The skill is a lab-focused network service guide, and many Markdown fence findings are false positives. Real risks remain from privileged commands, persistent service enablement, active enumeration commands, weak SNMP defaults, and anonymous writable SMB guidance. I found no prompt injection text or hidden obfuscation intent.

remediation.issue: Privileged host changes and service persistence
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running sudo, firewall, or systemctl commands. Mark service enablement as optional and include teardown steps.
Replace public and private examples with unique lab-only values or SNMPv3 guidance. Bind SNMP only to a private lab interface.
Avoid chmod 777 and guest writable shares by default. Use dedicated test users, narrow permissions, and cleanup instructions.
Add authorization checks, target scope confirmation, and warnings before nmap, enum4linux, smbmap, snmpwalk, or brute-force examples.

remediation.issue: Lab isolation depends on user discipline
remediation.suggestion: Add a required isolation checklist and explicit rollback steps for firewall rules, services, shares, and SNMP configuration.

semantic_findings.title: Weak SNMP Community Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs adding rocommunity public and rwcommunity private for SNMP. These default community strings can disclose or modify host data if the lab is reachable.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The weak community strings are present in SNMP configuration guidance. The file also restarts snmpd after adding them.

semantic_findings.title: Anonymous Writable SMB Share Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill configures guest SMB access with read-only disabled and world-writable directories. This can allow unauthorized file writes if used outside an isolated lab.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The SMB examples include chmod 777, guest access, and writable sharing. These settings are intentionally insecure for lab use.

semantic_findings.title: Lab Isolation Stated But Not Enforced
semantic_findings.description: The skill warns that labs should be isolated, but it also includes firewall allow rules and bind-all troubleshooting advice. The guidance relies on the user to prevent exposure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file states the isolation requirement and also suggests exposure-related changes. I did not find enforcement steps or cleanup gates.

content.value_statement: Network lab setup often requires many service, firewall, and enumeration steps. This skill organizes HTTP, HTTPS, SNMP, and SMB lab guidance for authorized testing.
actual_capabilities: Guides HTTP and HTTPS lab service setup on Linux and Windows hosts.
Shows self-signed certificate creation and HTTPS verification steps.
Explains SNMP service setup and common enumeration checks.
Explains SMB share setup and common SMB enumeration tools.
Provides port references, log review steps, and troubleshooting guidance.
limitations: The guidance includes insecure defaults intended only for isolated labs.
Many steps require administrative privileges and can change host configuration.
It does not provide automated rollback, scoping checks, or production hardening.
It assumes access to Linux, Windows Server, and security testing tools.

use_cases.title: Build a Training Lab
use_cases.description: Set up common network services in a disposable lab for enumeration practice.

use_cases.title: Prepare Class Exercises
use_cases.description: Create repeatable HTTP, SNMP, and SMB targets for authorized lessons.

use_cases.title: Validate Service Exposure
use_cases.description: Review service ports, firewall rules, and logs in a controlled test network.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up HTTP Practice
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline an authorized HTTP lab on a disposable Linux VM. Include prerequisites, safety checks, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add HTTPS Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan HTTPS testing with a self-signed certificate in an isolated lab. Explain what each step changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create SNMP Enumeration Lab
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an SNMP enumeration exercise for a private lab network. Include safe scoping and expected observations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Service Lab
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan HTTP, HTTPS, SNMP, and SMB targets for an authorized class lab. Include isolation, cleanup, and risk notes.

output_examples.input: Help me create an HTTP service lab on Ubuntu.
output: Confirms the lab is isolated before any host changes.
Lists required packages, firewall decisions, and service checks.
Explains how to verify the web service from the test machine.

output_examples.input: I need an SNMP enumeration exercise for students.
output: Defines the target host, community string scope, and test network limits.
Describes expected enumeration results without using production systems.
Adds cleanup steps to remove weak lab settings.

output_examples.input: Review my SMB lab plan for risks.
output: Flags anonymous access and broad write permissions as lab-only settings.
Recommends least privilege alternatives for safer demonstrations.

best_practices: Run examples only in isolated, disposable lab networks with explicit authorization.
Confirm every privileged command with the user before changing services or firewall rules.
Document setup, verification, and cleanup steps for each service.
anti_patterns: Do not run enumeration commands against networks without written permission.
Do not deploy weak SNMP or anonymous SMB settings on production hosts.
Do not leave lab services enabled after the exercise ends.

faq.question: What does this skill help configure?
faq.answer: It helps plan HTTP, HTTPS, SNMP, and SMB service labs for authorized security training.

faq.question: Is it safe for production systems?
faq.answer: No. Several examples use insecure lab settings and require administrative privileges.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides guidance. Any command should require clear user approval before execution.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What skills should the user have?
faq.answer: Users should understand IP addressing, ports, firewalls, and basic Linux or Windows administration.

faq.question: How should risky examples be handled?
faq.answer: Use a private lab, record the scope, and remove weak service settings after testing.
